full_judgment: 5. Mr. Sk Razzaque Ali the learned Advocate, has appeared in support of the Rule and he has in the first place contended that the learned Appellate Court failed to consider the documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiff in coming to a conclusion with regard to the real controversy between the parties in the suit. He has pointed out particularly from Exhibit 7, the kabala dated 28-3-1923 showing transfer of 0.92 decimals of land by Safaruddin Faraji to the father of the plaintiff and Exhibit 6(a) which indicates that Menhajuddin had been in possession of that portion of the land as purchaser and he had the under raiyati right which was inherited by him. He further contended that the document No. 6(a) having presumption of correctness has not been evaluated and the rent receipts Exhibit 3 series have not been considered along with the oral testimony in arriving at a finding of possession of plaintiff in the suit land and, consequently, there has been total misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence occasioning failure of justice. The 2nd branch of submission of Mr.Sk Razzaque Ali is that Kha schedule land which is the suit land comprises CS Khatian Nos. 688 and 689 constituted under- tenancy under CS Khatian No. 687 and there having no khas land, the auction purchaser Asmat Ali could not have acquired any title and interest in the land of Khatian Nos. 688 and 689 unless the under tenancy is annulled by service of notice as contemplated under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and he says that there is no proof of annulment of under tenancies and the tenant having Kolkarsha or Dar karsha right continued to be the tenant in the holdings and the plaintiff got title not on the basis of auction purchase but by way of inheritance and purchase from the original tenants. The courts below having not considered this aspect of the case committed error of law occasioning failure of justice and in this regard reliance has been made on different cases of Indian jurisdiction.
